newsitem.title: USA: Georgia-Pacific sees cost cuts impact post - Q1.
newsitem.headline: Georgia-Pacific sees cost cuts impact post - Q1.

text.p: Georgia-Pacific Corp said Thursday that $200 million in savings realized so far from a three-year cost-cutting effort would begin to show up on its bottom line sometime after the first quarter.
A company spokesman said the forest products manufacturer had completed the forced-layoff segment of the initiative after trimming 600 people from its payroll.

However, total job cuts were expected to reach 2,500 by the end of the program, compared with 1,600 currently, as Georgia-Pacific pressed ahead with more early retirement offers and eliminated more jobs through attrition.

Georgia-Pacific implemented the three-year cost-reduction plan last May, saying it intended to realize total savings of $400 million. Savings reached the $200 million half-way mark around the end of last year.

Company spokesman Ken Haldin, responding to a report in Thursday's Atlanta Journal-Constitution which said the savings realized so far would impact pretax earnings in the third quarter, said "It is during the course of '97 that we will realize that. To pinpoint it on one quarter would not be accurate, and certainly not in the first quarter. We just completed the last wave of the activity value analysis," he said.
